turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've just had you on the machine, blood pressure's 138 over 84, pulse 86. On the medication list I've got amlodipine ten milligrams.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten? Uh, no, I take five milligrams of amlodapine, I've stared at that bottle every morning. The chart's got me mixed up, I reckon, unless the chemist changed it and nobody told me.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. The list says ten and you're saying five, so I'm not writing a dose down till someone sights the bottle. Come and sit. What brought you in today?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, I booked because I need my own bloods sorted. I'm pregnant, sixteen weeks on Tuesday if I've counted right, and I feel like a wet rag. I've overdone it just walking up from the car park.

[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sixteen weeks, alright, I'll take that. The wet rag thing is tiredness, we'll park it for a minute. Was the pregnancy the whole reason, or did something else push you to book?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, so my husband went to a screening camp at work, the one the union ran, and they told him he carries the thalasemia trait. I'm anxious about the bub, properly anxious, and he's the same. I can't hear myself think with that waiting-room telly, it's up so loud.

[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so that result is his, not yours. Err, thinking it through, if he's a carrier the baby is only at real risk if you carry it as well, which is why the bloods matter. Did the slip say alpha or beta?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It didn't say, just trait, and the print was tiny. He got home, took his metformin because his tea was late, that's his sugar medicine, not mine, and then we just sat at the table worrying. I started reading forums and, well, one tab becomes twenty.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): His metformin stays his, I'm not putting that on your list. Before I disappear down the genetics, any shortness of breath?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, breathing's fine. It's my feet, they feel dead, both of them, like wood, especially at night. And there's a frog in my throat most mornings, I keep clearing it, it's been annoying.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Both feet, and the throat. Any spotting or bleeding?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No bleeding, nothing. Umm, the frog, I can't tell you when that started, a week, maybe more, I really don't know. The feet, that's been a couple of weeks, give or take.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any swelling in the face or the hands? And the waterworks, any burning, anything off in that system?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling. Waterworks, no burning, they're normal apart from me peeing more, which I think is just the pregnancy. Sorry, I always add the extra clause, my sister says I can't answer in one word.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): More wees can just be sixteen weeks, I'm not calling that an infection. Ankles aren't puffy. Throat's a little red, nothing dramatic.

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. My sister, while I'm on her, she takes biotin for her hair, huge capsules, that's hers, I don't touch it, and her shoes are a whole other saga. Not relevant, I know, I just talk.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not yours, we'll leave it. What do you actually take, in your own words, with the doses and when?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine for the pressure, in the morning, and I still say five milligrams not ten. The cholesterol one at night, twenty milligrams, I swallow it, I can never remember the name, little white oval. Sugar tablets, five hundred milligrams, one in the morning and one with tea, and only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, one teaspoon stirred into warm water.

[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the pressure, I'm hearing hypertension, that's why the amlodipine, and I won't quiz you on cholesterol or sugar because you haven't named those conditions and I'm not inventing them. The powder I'd rather you hold while you're pregnant. And that unnamed cholesterol tablet, I'd stop it, statins and pregnancy don't sit well even when I can't see the brand.

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, I'll stop the cholesterol one from tonight, and I'll leave the powder in the cupboard. The sugar tablets I keep, yeah? They're not metformin, that's my husband's, mine just say 500 on the foil. I take them properly, I think, except I forget the tea-time one some days when I'm out.

[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the sugar tablets, same five hundred, morning and with tea, and bring the box so we can actually name them. Forgetting the tea-time one some days, I'll mark that as not sure you're taking them as prescribed. Amlodipine, stay on whatever the bottle says, I'm not changing the pressure treatment on a mismatched dose.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Bottle's on the fridge, I'll bring it. I've been on the pressure tablets since before this pregnancy, we just never say hypertension at home, it's always the pressure. The Ayurvedic one I got from the grocer in Footscray, the man said it was for energy, but I'll leave it.

[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): I can book the bloods at the desk when you leave. Full blood count and the haemoglobin electroferesis, is that the pair? And do you want genetic counselling booked as well or not yet?

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Book the full blood count and the haemoglobin electrophoresis, yes, today if they can, to see whether she carries the trait too. Don't book counselling yet. If the electrophoresis shows she's a carrier as well, then we refer her for genetic counselling, and if it doesn't, we don't.

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): So counselling only if I'm a carrier too, otherwise we breathe out. I've been on forums till midnight, which doesn't help, I know. I'll try to stop doing that, I always over-read.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's the branch. My working impression, provisional only, is that your husband is a thalassaemia carrier on that camp test and we don't know your status, so I can't call this pregnancy high risk or low risk yet. Alpha or beta, either's still possible, the slip didn't separate them.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. And the tiredness, me feeling like a wet rag, you don't reckon that's me already having the trait?

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't hang the tiredness on thalassaemia without the bloods. Numb feet and the frog in the throat, I'll note them, but let's see what the tests say before I name a cause. That's not a diagnosis from me.

[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): I'll put those two blood tests through for this afternoon if pathology can fit you, otherwise tomorrow morning. And a review back here in two weeks for the results. That alright?

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Two weeks, book that review regardless. Bring the amlodipine bottle and the sugar-tablet box with you. If something feels wrong before then you can ring, but the appointment stands.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, I'll be here, both boxes. Cholesterol tablet skipped from tonight, powder stays in the cupboard. If my feet get worse or I start spotting I'll ring, you don't have to make a speech of it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll say it anyway, ring if the feet get worse or there's any spotting. Otherwise I see you in two weeks with those bloods, and we go from there.

spec.situation: Couple, wife pregnant, husband found to carry thalassaemia trait at a camp; both anxious; blood tests for the wife planned; genetic counselling discussed.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Husband's trait is not family history as stated; transcript reports spouse result only.
Morning throat symptom is reported, but hoarseness specifically is not stated.
bad.text: hoarseness (category=ENT, status=present, frequency=most mornings, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose recorded by the patient as 5 mg each morning; current medications entry lacks the dose despite the explicit patient report and dose discrepancy discussion.
The doctor advised the unnamed cholesterol tablet should be stopped specifically because statins and pregnancy do not sit well, even though the brand was unknown.
The patient confirmed she would stop the cholesterol tablet from tonight and stop the Ayurvedic powder, and that the powder had been bought from a grocer in Footscray for energy.
The patient has been on the blood pressure tablets since before this pregnancy.
Review timing detail: blood tests were to be arranged for this afternoon if possible, otherwise tomorrow morning.
Conditional plan detail: genetic counselling should not be booked yet; refer only if haemoglobin electrophoresis shows she is also a carrier, and not if it does not.
